I've farmed these 18 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, since I was 15. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and sometimes I go to the village meetings when the extension people come, but honestly I trust what I see in my own field and what the good farmers around me do more than anything on paper. My son works in a factory in Handan, so it's just me and my husband managing the land now. We have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but labor is tight — if we fall behind on planting or spraying, the whole year is ruined.

Last year my wheat made about 540 kg per mu and maize about 620 kg. This year I will do almost the same, maybe push fertilizer a little because the dealer said compound fertilizer is a bit cheaper, and I would rather spend a bit more than risk losing yield — a bad harvest means no money for my son's wedding next year. For winter wheat, I will rotary till the soil in October and sow improved seed, the same kind my neighbor used last year and got a full harvest. I put almost one 50-kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing — that gives about 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu — and at jointing I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu, which adds another 9 kg of nitrogen. I irrigate three times: overwinter water in early December, jointing water in late March, and one more at heading in early May. I spray three times — herbicide in early spring, then a fungicide and insecticide mix twice later when I see aphids and rust. For summer maize, right after wheat harvest in June I plant hybrid seed without tilling because there is no time to waste — if you miss the sowing window by even a few days, yield drops badly. I put about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing and 25 kg of urea at big trumpet stage. I irrigate three times — right after sowing, at jointing, and at grain filling. Two sprays: one herbicide at seedling stage and one insecticide when I see worms. I expect 550 kg per mu for wheat and 650 kg per mu for maize.
